evidence: Cic. Or. 70: poēmata opposed to ōrātiō (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 30: poēma, poēmatis n., a poem
terms.comment: Poetry as a body of poems; the singular poēma, poēmatis n. is one poem.

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 4.69: ō praeclāram ēmendātrīcem vītae poēticam! (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Poetry as an art or pursuit; Nepos and Pliny use the Greek form poēticē, poēticēs f..

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 4.71: Anacreontis tōta poēsis est amātōria (Lewis & Short)

terms.comment: Poems, especially as songs; the word for one’s own verses (see song). versūs facere is “write poetry” (Cic. Q. fr. 3.5, Lewis & Short s.v. faciō).

phrases.latin: sponte suā carmen numerōs veniēbat ad aptōs, et quod temptābam scrībere versus erat
phrases.english: of its own accord my song fell into the right rhythm, and whatever I tried to write came out as verse

phrases.latin: foliīs tantum nē carmina mandā, nē turbāta volent rapidīs lūdibria ventīs
phrases.english: only don’t write your verses on leaves, in case they are scattered and fly off as playthings of the rushing winds

sources: Lewis & Short: poema · Lewis & Short: poeticus · Lewis & Short: poesis · Lewis & Short: carmen
